comment: Every version QGSDK installs, in one place. The scripts and CI read this file; change a version here, nowhere else. Grouped by profile: install the ones you work on (qgsdk install --profile ...). See docs/manifest.md.

python.comment: QGSDK's own tooling runs on this Python, whatever the profile. It ships with QGSDK and never with an application. No installer, no admin rights, nothing written outside the prefix. Windows: python.org's official build, as its NuGet package (a zip). Linux and macOS: python-build-standalone, the relocatable CPython build uv uses (a tarball); the system Python is never used. Keyed by platform and machine (uname -m).

aqtinstall.comment: Installs Qt and its tools without a Qt account. Pinned to a commit: Qt 6.11 changed its repository layout and no release since 3.3.0 reads it (docs/decisions/0002).
aqtinstall.version_comment: A source zip has no git history, so the version aqtinstall would read from git is given here (SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION). No git needed on the machine.

logger.description: QSO Graph Logger: Qt, the compiler, CMake and Ninja, and NSIS for the Windows installer

linux.comment: Built with GCC; the compiler is the system's (any GCC with C++17), with the OpenGL, EGL and xkbcommon headers Qt's CMake files look for. The bootstrap checks for them; QGSDK never installs system packages.

macos.comment: A universal build (Apple silicon and Intel). The compiler is Apple's clang from the Xcode command-line tools, which the bootstrap checks for and never installs.

windows.name: MinGW
windows.comment: Qt's MinGW binaries are ABI-matched to this compiler. Mixing versions gives crashes that look like application bugs.

downloads.comment: Tools that don't come from Qt's repositories: downloaded from their publisher, checked against the SHA-256 here, unpacked under <prefix>/tools/<name>.

windows.name: NSIS
windows.comment: Makes QGLogger's Windows installer (CPack's NSIS generator). The portable zip: no installer, no admin rights. SHA-256 taken from the download, which matched the SHA-1 SourceForge publishes for it.

mcp.description: qso-graph's MCP servers: uv, the Python versions they test against, and git
mcp.python_versions_comment: Installed by uv into the prefix (UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR): the versions the servers' CI tests. Which patch release each one is follows from the pinned uv. No 3.10: it reaches end of life in October 2026, and its Windows build carries OpenSSL 1.1.1 (qso-graph/.github#39).

downloads.comment: Downloaded from the publisher, checked against the SHA-256 here, unpacked under <prefix>/tools/<name>. An entry with "machine" applies only on that machine (uname -m: arm64, x86_64). On Linux and macOS git comes from the system (the Xcode command-line tools on macOS).

windows.name: MinGit
windows.comment: Git for Windows' portable build: no installer, no admin rights.
